scanTooltip: Open the CodeBuddy login window and capture the credential after you scan
scanNeedsProtocol: No loginUrl in the protocol yet: click through and you'll be pointed to Protocol config, or paste the credential instead
scanWaiting: Scan and authorise in that window — {{seconds}}s left
scanConfirm: Credential captured — review it before storing
scanFailed: Could not capture a credential automatically
scanNotOpened: The login window could not be opened
scanTimeout: Timed out: no usable credential was seen in the login window.
scanTruncated: The captured value exceeded the transfer ceiling — paste it manually instead.
scanStats: Capture script alive · {{calls}} requests observed · {{auth}} with auth headers · session check {{probe}}
scanCookieNotLoggedIn: The login window is still on the login page: sign in there first, then try again.
scanCookieUnusable: No usable session cookie in the login window (empty or over the ceiling) — reload that page and retry.

scanHelp.opening: The login window is opening — scan the QR code with the CodeBuddy app.
scanHelp.waiting: After sign-in the capture script grabs the login token from the sign-in response body (bearer JWT, measured as replayable); the window then jumps to the “API Keys” page for reference. Once the credential shows up here, review and store it; cookies are only grabbed automatically after the in-page session check passes.
scanHelp.verifying: The credential is written to the local SQLite database (plaintext, like Cursor / model keys) and immediately probed.
scanHelp.confirming: Nothing is stored yet: check the name and credential, then hit “Add to pool”.
scanHelp.saved: Add another account, or finish and return to the pool.
scanHelp.failed: Auto-capture relies on the page putting a token into a request header or response body (the web session is httpOnly cookies, which page scripts cannot read). If nothing shows up, “Paste credential” works just as well; if the login window never opened, set loginUrl in Protocol config first.

captureNote: Captured from the login window (via {{via}}). Rename it or replace the value before storing.
captureCookieWarn: This is a browser session cookie: measured as non-replayable (requests carrying it get back exactly what an unauthenticated request gets), and the probe only accepts a bearer JWT. The capture script also grabs the real Keycloak JWT from the sign-in response body (type token) — store that one, not the cookie.
label: Name
credentialHint: Stored in the local SQLite database (plaintext, like Cursor / model keys). Never uploaded.
credentialEditHint: Leave empty to keep the current credential.
deleteConfirmMessage: Remove “{{label}}” and its locally stored credential? This cannot be undone.
emptyBody: Use “Scan to add” above to capture a credential from the login window, or paste one manually.
protocolHint: Login page, check-in and chat endpoints are configured here as JSON. Save before accounts can be verified.
protocolMissing: No protocol configured — accounts stay unverified
protocolDocProbe: credentialProbe: checks a credential is still alive
protocolDocChat: chat: upstream the gateway proxies to; {model} is substituted
probeHint: Don't know the upstream URLs? Open the login window, sign in, then hit “Read calls” to see which backend endpoints the page itself calls — pick a row to write it into the config below.
probeReadHint: Click around inside the login window (the API keys page in particular), then come back and hit “Read calls”. Try a row first: 2xx in the browser but 401 on replay means the session cannot leave the browser — switch to a bearer token.
probeEmpty: No API calls captured: the login window is probably still on the login page, or it navigated away.
probeApplied: Wrote this endpoint into {{target}} — save once it looks right.
probeTryHint: Have the page inside the login window re-issue this request to see whether it works with the browser’s own session — it separates “wrong endpoint” from “credential cannot leave the browser”
gatewayLanWarning: Other machines on your network could use your account pool. Configure keys and the IP allowlist first.
fieldRequired: Name and credential are both required
gatewayStoppedHint: Stopped: start it, then point workbuddy2api at the port above.
gatewayBindLocal: Listening on 127.0.0.1 only — unreachable from other machines.
gatewayBindLan: Listening on 0.0.0.0: reachable on your LAN. Make sure keys and IP rules are set.
gatewayLanConfirm: Enabling this restarts the gateway bound to 0.0.0.0.
gatewayLanUrlHint: Other machines on the LAN: keep the port, replace 127.0.0.1 with this machine's LAN IP.
keyLabelRequired: Give the key a label first
keyShownOnce: This key is shown only once — copy it now
keyResetConfirm: Rotate the secret for “{{label}}”? The old one stops working immediately.
keyResetWarning: Every client still using the old key will start receiving 401s.
keyDeleteConfirm: Delete “{{label}}” ({{count}} calls)? Clients using it will be rejected immediately.
keysEmpty: No keys yet. The gateway requires Authorization: Bearer wk-…, so create one.
ipEmpty: No rules: in LAN mode every non-local address is allowed by default.
ipHintLocal: The gateway is bound to 127.0.0.1, so remote addresses cannot connect and these rules are inert until LAN mode is on.
ipHintLan: The gateway is open to the LAN: a deny match rejects outright, and any enabled allow rule turns the default into “deny everything else”.
ipFirewallHint: Windows prompts for firewall access the first time it binds 0.0.0.0; to keep it open permanently use the command below (needs admin — this app never runs it for you).
logClearWarning: Usage stats drop to zero with it; the running gateway is unaffected.
logEmpty: No calls yet. Start the gateway and hit /v1/chat/completions with an issued key.
checkinClearConfirm: Clear all {{count}} check-in rows? Per-account fail counters are kept.
checkinHint: Accounts are checked in serially with a 2s gap to reduce risk-control exposure; 5 consecutive failures disable an account.
checkinNoEndpoint: The protocol has no checkin endpoint; check-in is disabled. Fill the template in Protocol settings to enable it.
checkinNoAccounts: No enabled accounts to check in.
checkinNothingToDo: Nothing to check in (all disabled or expired).
checkinAutoDisabled: “{{label}}” hit the failure limit and was disabled
checkinStatusNotConfigured: No checkinStatus endpoint in the protocol; fill in the template under Protocol to enable.
growthNotConfigured: No growth endpoints in the protocol; fill in the template under Protocol to enable.
growthNoData: Pick an account and press Query to see the streak ladder and tasks.
growthRedeemNote: Read-only display; redeem and claim in the official client — this app never redeems.
